purpose: Revised A garden-path raster proposals responding to insufficient grandeur. Three distinct monumental landscape compositions.

prompts.A1:
Create a radically more awe-inspiring revision of the attached ADELVA garden-path website mockup, as ONE final-quality photographic desktop web SECTION mock image, portrait approximately 1536x2048. The reference supplies ONLY the accepted concept of a garden footpath connecting hospitality buildings, a continuous scroll-progress line, and exact brand/section/stage text. The user rejected the reference's intimate scale and lack of grandeur. You are authorized to completely replace camera distance, landscape, composition and header treatment. Do NOT repeat a close drone shot of a small ryokan garden.
VISUAL PRIORITY: a monumental landscape with extraordinary spatial depth and scale, tiny believable architecture as a scale cue, and 40–50% calm negative space. Think a painstakingly composed large-format aerial landscape photograph on a cinematic hospitality website. Show nature several hundred meters across and tiny maintained footpaths, not an ordinary hotel's backyard. The physical walkway remains a WALKABLE garden route within one expansive hospitality landscape, not a highway, dangerous mountain trail or magical floating bridge. Original fictional place, real-world gravity, convincing geology and architecture, sophisticated controlled photographic exposure. Single coherent light and time. Avoid fantasy concept-art, glowing portals, epic movie matte painting, excessive sun rays, oversaturated turquoise, snowy mountains, polar maps, airplanes, giant resorts or multiple photo panels.
WEB DESIGN: one edge-to-edge full-bleed photo occupying almost the entire image; no separate large cream header that reduces the landscape. At top place a small widely spaced 'ADELVA', the exact refined serif heading 'From Strategy to Action', and Japanese '支援の進め方'. Title fits elegantly in calm negative space; photograph is the overwhelming visual protagonist. No other marketing copy, nav, buttons, badges or claims. Preserve SIX legible Japanese stages in order down the long scene, exactly once each: '01 課題把握', '02 判断', '03 実行・実装', '04 運用', '05 検証', '06 引継ぎ'. Use restrained off-white Japanese sans-serif, generous separation, never huge numbered cards. A very fine muted warm-ivory/gold overlay line guides the eye roughly top-to-bottom through the garden landscape from a small entrance pavilion toward a small hospitality lodge; it follows a plausible route on LAND or a supported walkway. Six small nodes, one near 04 slightly bright. Photograph must supply room for labels; no textual boxes. The graphic is a delicate UI overlay, NOT neon illuminating the physical environment. No additional text. Retain hospitality and the connected garden path as the central meaning. Grand scale comes from framing, void, topography and small human-scale architecture, not a cluttered spectacle.
A1: MONUMENTAL GRANITE GARDEN AND FOREST. Very high oblique aerial view into an immense sheltered basin formed by two great natural granite escarpments, sculptural pale weathered rock faces hundreds of meters across, sparse dark pines, elegant broad moss/meadow gardens at their bases. At upper left a tiny entrance pavilion. A narrow but visible pale stone garden walk descends in a long graceful S through the sheltered basin, with low stone borders and occasional carefully maintained terraces, to a tiny horizontal timber-and-stone lodge at lower right, almost dwarfed by the rocks. The lodge occupies only 5–7% of image width; one understated warm opening establishes human scale. Great sheer rocks rise near left and upper edges, their textures visible at many scales. A deep graphite negative-space zone of shaded rock and low still mist in center-right makes thin type readable; mist does NOT erase the path. Soft early morning sidelight, silver-gray rock, charcoal forest, restrained olive moss, extraordinary real photographic depth. No jagged fantasy spikes, alpine snow, enormous waterfall or dangerous exposed footpath. This is an expansive landscape garden and retreat, visibly cultivated in subtle ways, not a hiking advertisement. Frame like an actual aerial architectural landscape photograph, never a miniature model.

A2: WATER MIRROR GARDEN. An immense near-black perfectly still lake fills 50% of a high aerial composition, with a towering forested rocky shore occupying one side and reflected layers of pale soft mist giving vast atmospheric depth. A long narrow landscaped peninsula curves elegantly from upper left toward lower center into the mirror water, its pale stone GARDEN FOOTPATH connected continuously along the LAND of the peninsula. Small supported footbridges can bridge only a short channel, no giant unsupported causeway. Carefully tended low grasses, a few dark pines and exposed stone emphasize Japanese hospitality landscape design. A tiny entry pavilion at upper left and a low original timber-and-stone lodge tucked into the peninsula's lower end, 5–7% image width, with a tiny warm-lit slit. Keep most lake EMPTY and still, almost abstract dark graphite with exceptionally subtle reflections; the sweeping peninsula/path and single lodge are strongly readable against it. Broad scale, no close garden pond, no swimming pool, no tea-house illustration. Viewpoint sufficiently overhead that the whole path can be followed down the screen. Fine route line adjacent to that path; place labels primarily over dark water with subtle short visual alignment to their nodes. Large soft morning atmosphere, delicate physical textures. A world-class landscape photograph made quiet through enormous emptiness, not darkness alone.

review.all: All returned raster previews visually reviewed. Exact English title, Japanese section title and six Japanese stage labels present. Connected landscaped paths, hospitality buildings and distinct large landscape compositions visible. Fictional conceptual facilities, not client evidence.
review.A1: Rock-face framing creates the strongest vertical mass and enclosure. More image detail and less negative space than A2.
review.A2: Largest calm water field and clearest landscape/line separation. Recommended balance of scale, stillness and legibility.
review.A3: Most open coastal depth. Additional unlabelled terminal dot is illustrative; route geometry requires authored SVG if implemented.
